interest: This docket sheet illustrates the U.S. government's systematic monitoring of Japanese gold policy during the 1930s, a critical period marked by military expansion and mounting foreign exchange strains. It highlights Japan's efforts to stimulate domestic gold mining, enforce government gold-purchasing regulations, and ultimately draw down bank gold reserves for export to fund wartime imports during the Second Sino-Japanese War. Furthermore, it provides valuable archival utility by tracing cross-references to other State Department economic and financial files (notably decimal file 894.515), demonstrating how commercial, consular, and military attachés coordinated economic intelligence reporting.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.6341, 'Mines. Mining. Concessions., Precious Metals And Precious Stones., Japan, Gold') consists of a single-page State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexing four records produced between 1934 and 1939 concerning Japanese gold mining, policy, and reserves. The recorded entries include an April 1934 notification from Commercial Attaché Frank S. Williams in Tokyo regarding regulations governing Japan's Gold Purchasing Law; a July 19 report from the U.S. Military Attaché in Japan regarding plans to increase domestic gold production; a September 1939 report from Consul Louis E. Gourley in Kobe analyzing Japan's gold situation; and a December 1939 report from Kobe reporting that Japan was expediting gold exports and drawing down bank gold reserves. Three of the four entries include cross-reference notes redirecting researchers to other State Department files (102.81 Tokyo/34 and 894.515).

subfiles.about: A State Department docket sheet indexing four communications regarding Japanese gold mining, purchasing regulations, production initiatives, and export of gold reserves between 1934 and 1939.
subfiles.summary: This document serves as the official State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for subject file 894.6341, tracking documents on gold mining and precious metals in Japan. It catalogues four communications recorded between April 1934 and December 1939 from the Commercial Attaché in Tokyo, the Military Attaché in Japan, and the American Consulate in Kobe. The entries document the 1934 Gold Purchasing Law regulations published in the Official Gazette, military intelligence on production expansion programs, general surveys of the gold situation, and late-1939 measures speeding up gold shipments while depleting bank reserves. Cross-reference notations direct researchers to related files 102.81 Tokyo/34 and 894.515.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Gold Mining in Japan (File 894.6341)
